text:
ana: Quick sync — drafting a lighter-weight launch checklist for private deployments that targets customers who need controlled upgrades but not full BGP automation. Goal: reduce upgrade blasts and provide clear rollback steps. Anyone heard new field asks?

mike: saw a request from Acme Corp — they want predictable maintenance windows and an "upgrade handshake" so their NetOps can sign off. basically they need a pause/resume token for upgrades.

devon: pause/resume token makes sense. we should also include a dry-run mode for the installer where it outputs proposed route changes as a manifest without applying them.

sam.k: for dry-run, we can generate a diff of BGP table changes and estimate traffic shift. low-effort telemetry: sample 1% of sessions to validate route path in staging.

irene: propose three launch gates: 1) installer dry-run validated in customer's staging 2) routing revert validated (automated revert script) 3) egress-cost warning and opt-in 

ana: define "validated" — i'd say runbook-confirmed + two successful dry-run passes across different topologies (single-AZ, cross-AZ).

mike: on rollback UX—should be a single CLI command `redwood rollback-routing --to=prev` and a web console button that triggers same. Need idempotency guards.

sam.k: experiments: run controlled failover with traffic replay and assert no more than 0.1% 5xx errors. put that in acceptance criteria.

deploy-bot: RELEASE NOTE: installer v1.8.0 includes dry-run flag --dry-run-route-check

ana: actions: ana update checklist doc, devon add handshake token to API spec, sam.k run experiment plan by Mon, irene draft UX copy for console opt-in, mike mock CLI rollback. i'll schedule a 20m review Fri.

devon: +1. also: we should add a customer-visible log of route changes for audit (and ticketing).

ana: good call. audit trail required for compliance-sensitive customers. adding to docs.

mike: I'll ping Acme to offer staged pilot next week.
